effect: The final result shows how touch signals and muscle tension help steady a slipping glass, completing the chapter's goals.
reaction: The slipping-glass sequence made the feedback loop concrete and satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Holding the glass brought the skin, nerves and muscles together in a recognizable task. The sequence explains why holding something still requires active work.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the supporting and surface layers was straightforward, but the successive joining steps felt somewhat repetitive. The tugging descriptions helped distinguish what each layer contributed.

surprise.text: I found the distinction between dead outer skin cells and the living layers that replace them informative.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the item descriptions and goals gave each combination a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it built toward another everyday action. The glass example made the relationships between systems more engaging than assembling layers alone.
